messages:
ethan: morning - found 6 snapshots in prod encrypted with SSE-C (customer-provided keys) instead of SSE-KMS. headers show x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256 and x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-key-md5 present.
claire: SSE-C? we never configure uploader to use SSE-C. do we persist customer keys anywhere?
mohit: whoa. uploader accepts SSE env var from tenant config. seems a tenant-level migration test accidentally toggled `USE_SSE_C=true` in the deploy for tenant-63 and a loop in batch upload applied it across a shard.
ethan: list of affected objects: backups/2026-04-02/tenant-63/snap-001.tar.gz, snap-002.tar.gz, backups/2026-04-02/tenant-64/snap-003.tar.gz (mis-sharded), plus 3 more.
security-bot: audit: 6 objects with SSE-C header between 2026-04-02T01:10:00Z and 2026-04-02T01:20:00Z. No CloudTrail GetObject activity aside from internal re-checks. flagged SEV-3.
claire: problem: SSE-C requires the customer key to decrypt. uploader never persisted the CPK to our vault (we don't store plaintext customer keys). if tenant didn't provide key material to us persistently, those objects are unrecoverable to us.
oncall-sre: containment: block any further uploads that set x-amz-server-side-encryption to AES256 with x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-key-* headers. I'll push a bucket policy deny for PutObject when SSE-C headers are present.
opsbot: runbook executed: applied bucket policy to deny SSE-C PutObject on s3://redwood-prod-archives at 2026-04-02T01:35:12Z. Created INC-6021.
mohit: why did uploader accept this flag? there was a CV for a tenant emergency where they provided a one-time SSE-C key in POST meta, and a later patch's retry logic accidentally cached the header in the batch iterator. config bug.
ethan: immediate question: can we decrypt these objects? any chance the CPK was logged or proxied to our ingress?
claire: searching logs: we explicitly sanitize the CPK value before persistence, but for a 2hr window a debugging flag `LOG_SENSITIVE=false` was mis-set and part of the request body including a base64 customer key appears in ephemeral logs on a single ingestion pod. logs rotated; we have one ephemeral node snapshot that might contain the CPK.
security-bot: found one ingress log file on pod backup-ingest-5 dated 2026-04-02T01:12:03Z that contains header `x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-key: <BASE64_KEY_REDACTED>` in plain. immediate forensics required.
oncall-sre: do not grep logs casually. we need to maintain chain-of-custody. creating forensics run INF-6021-FOR and locking node image.
opsbot: forensic task created and node snapshot preserved at 2026-04-02T01:40:00Z. ticket INF-6021-FOR.
mohit: if we can retrieve the base64 key, we could re-download the objects and decrypt locally using `--sse-c` param then re-upload with SSE-KMS. example:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-archives/backups/.../snap-001.tar.gz ./snap-001.tar.gz --sse-c AES256 --sse-c-key <base64key>
aws s3 cp ./snap-001.tar.gz s3://redwood-prod-archives/.../snap-001.tar.gz --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd-ef12
```
ethan: does retrieving CPK from node logs violate policy? compliance/legal needs to approve.
compliance: we need a minimal access request. if the only way to restore customer data is to extract their CPK from ephemeral logs, we must notify affected tenants and get explicit approval before accessing secrets. prepare notification draft.
claire: we should still check if tenants provided an out-of-band key to support. some did via our secure portal; query tenant-63 key vault entries.
security-bot: tenant vault query: tenant-63 has no stored SSE-C keys; tenant-64 has a key but it is different from the one in the ephemeral log.
mohit: worst-case: if the key only exists in that ephemeral log and tenant doesn't approve access, we can't decrypt or re-encrypt on their behalf. we'll need to discuss data-loss SLA.
oncall-sre: forensics team obtained the base64 CPK from node snapshot under controlled access. storing in FIPS container for a short window. access logged.
compliance: legal reviewed and approved temporary retrieval for incident remediation with tenant notification. tenants notified draft prepared; waiting on PR approval to send. ticket INF-6021 updated.
ethan: planned remediation steps: 1) retrieve CPK from forensic snapshot (done) 2) stream-download objects with `--sse-c` using recovered key in ephemeral secure runner 3) re-upload with SSE-KMS using CMK 4) verify sha256 and ETAGs 5) purge any logs containing the CPK and produce redaction proof 6) harden uploader to disallow SSE-C in prod unless tenant-managed vault present.
mohit: running re-decrypt-and-reupload job now in isolated runner. will report checksum diffs.
opsbot: job started at 2026-04-02T02:10:00Z under ticket INF-6021.
security-bot: recommended long-term guards: - block SSE-C in prod by default - require tenant-managed key vault for SSE-C with explicit onboarding flow - add CI lint to prevent debug flags that could leak secrets - add daily audit rule for any objects with SSE-C header
claire: creating infra PR to add bucket enforcement and uploader validation. link: https://git.internal/infra/terraform/pulls/523
ethan: update: reupload completed at 2026-04-02T02:28:30Z. checksums verified, SSE-KMS metadata present. old SSE-C objects retained for now until we get tenant sign-off for destruction.
compliance: tenant notifications sent at 2026-04-02T02:45Z with explanation and remediation steps. tenants acknowledged.
oncall-sre: closing actions: revoke temporary forensic access, rotate any keys used by the node, merge uploader validation PR, and add SEV-3 alarm on SSE-C in prod. INF-6021 will remain open for 7 days for postmortem.
ethan: good work everyone. please attach reupload logs and redaction proof to INF-6021.
